index.html.lead: Home says what Ordinance DS is and what it enforces today.

topics.title: How to read this page
text: Clause 2 lists every rule that the check enforces. Clause 3 lists what is not built.

topics.title: The word checked
text: A page says checked only for a rule that the check enforces.

get-started.html.lead: This page takes you from the folder to a built and checked site.

topics.title: What you need
text: You need Node.js 20 or later. The browser test also needs Chrome or Edge.

topics.title: If the check fails
text: Read the first line. It names the rule in brackets, then the file, then the reason.

core.html.lead: The core is what every site built on Ordinance DS has.

topics.title: Core or plugin
text: A part is in the core when the site cannot build without it. Every other part is a plugin.

topics.title: Status
text: Built means that the part exists and the check covers it.

excluded.html.lead: This page lists what Ordinance DS leaves out on purpose.

topics.title: Why a list of what is missing
text: A reader can trust a framework more when it says where it stops.

css.html.lead: This page lists the layers and every token of the stylesheet.

topics.title: Tokens
text: A token is a named value, such as a colour or a size. A rule in the stylesheet uses the name, never the value.

topics.title: Themes
text: The system of the reader chooses the light or the dark theme.

parts.html.lead: This page shows each part and lists every registered name.

topics.title: A part
text: A part is a block of HTML with a registered class.

topics.title: State
text: A part shows a state with an attribute, such as `data-tone`. It never uses a class for a state.

plugins.html.lead: This page lists the plugins of this build and says how to write one.

topics.title: A plugin
text: A plugin is one folder that adds pages, styles or checks.

topics.title: Permissions
text: A plugin lists what it uses. The check compares the list with what the plugin does.

secure-by-default.html.lead: This page says what the pages refuse, and which headers a server sends.

topics.title: Inline code
text: Inline code is a style or a script that is written into a page. Ordinance DS has none, so the policy needs no exception.

topics.title: The headers
text: The table is written from the same file that the local server reads.

privacy.html.lead: This page says what a page of Ordinance DS tells other servers about its reader: nothing.

topics.title: Why it matters
text: A request to another server gives that server the address of the reader.

resilience.html.lead: This page says what a reader still gets when a part of a page fails.

topics.title: The idea
text: The words and the tables of a page never depend on a script.

accessibility.html.lead: This page says which accessibility rules are built in, and which a person must still test.

topics.title: Contrast
text: The contrast ratio compares a text colour with its surface. The check measures each pair.

topics.title: Criteria
text: The numbers are success criteria of WCAG 2.2.

checks.html.lead: This page lists every rule of the check and the other tests.

topics.title: One list
text: The rules are in one file. This page and the page Home are written from it.

topics.title: A failure
text: A failure starts with the name of the rule in brackets.

patterns.html.lead: This page shows whole pages that are made from the parts.

topics.title: Made-up data
text: The names, numbers and dates in the patterns are examples. They describe no real organisation.

topics.title: Use a pattern
text: Copy the markup of a pattern into a page of your plugin. Then build and check.

tables.html.lead: This page shows every variant of the table part.

topics.title: Made-up data
text: The rows in these tables are examples. They describe no real organisation.

topics.title: Which size to use
text: Use the compact size for a list that the reader scans. Use the roomy size for a few rows that the reader must read with care.
